newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast lt. crudes firm, diffs idle on Tue.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast lt. crudes firm, diffs idle on Tue.

text.p: U.S West Coast light crudes firmed with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) late Tuesday, with differentials flat as players stayed out of the market to assess April supply needs, traders said.
Discounts for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude remained at -$0.90 cents under WTI, with BP Oil Co declining to offer a price for the grade.
Outright prices stood $19.75/19.95, up 50 cents on the heels of technical buying in NYMEX crude.
Buyers of Line 63 attended the auction of light California grades from the Elk Hills Naval Petroleum Reserve on Tuesday.
Koch was the higher bidder for a 29,300 barrels-per-day offering of crude from the U.S. government field, priced on a posted index.
The company bid $20.2319 for 4,057 bpd of crude from the 18G zone. Bids were for a six-month delivery period starting April 1.
63 prices stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05.
Elk Hills crudes, produced in the middle of the state, are components of blended Line 63, which is shipped to Los Angeles refineries.
Other bidders, in descending order were: Bravo Energy at $20.1742 for 4,010 bpd, and Kern Oil at $20.1430 for 8,000 bpd
Kern River heavy crude prices fell, after a major California oil company lowered postings 50 cents late Monday, but no new deals were done.
